questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: The academic quality and reputation of the ETH Zürich.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The university is great and the academic level lived up to expectations.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Everything was neatly organized in a slideshow from ETH, there was no info lacking and I had virtually no need to seek additional information anywhere.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I registered at the university but did not receive any further assistance. I am sure that plenty of assistance is necessary if need be though.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: I found housing by doing a room swap with an outgoing ETH student who was going to Copenhagen. ETH gave me the contact details, and everything went super smoothly from there.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Bring your bike! The tram can get you anywhere but Zürich is also surprisingly good for cycling. The city center is expensive, so you are probably going to live some distance away, and it is thus a good idea to bring a bike.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: My housing situation was great - I am not certain it is so great for other students. If you land a room offer from the university in the Autumn semester you will be kicked out before end of exam season. Also, be out in good time - Zürich can be extremely expensive.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: You register online. Had no trouble.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: At ETH, the first week of courses is free-for-all, hence no course registration is binding until middle of the second week of semester. At this point you lock in your courses in a online web-portal similar to KUnet.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: I had trouble registering for one course, wrote to the exchange department who forwarded me to the math department, who asked me to get permission from the lecturer to take the course. He replied very fast and immediately got admitted. The whole process took around 30 min.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I managed to register for all of them. Be aware that if you want to do seminars there are limited spaces and should be out in good time.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Be out in good time if you want to do seminars, use the first week to browse courses.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The level taught is high and fast-paced. It is per say not more difficult than UCPH, but the pacing is faster and hence more material is covered per ECTS credit. I would say that a 3-5 credit course at ETH easily corresponds to a 7.5 UCPH course. Exams are a bit ridicolous as they are often designed to be unsolvable in the allotted time due to the sheer volume of problems on the exam, which can be a bit stressful (even though the problems are not necessarily difficult).

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Lectures are more or less the same. Less time is spend on formally proviing things and instead conveying intuition/covering more material. The students are however still expected to know the corresponding proofs. Contrary to at the math department at UCPH, excersise classes are utterly useless at ETH.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Numerical Solutions of Stochastic Ordinary Differential Equations
Causality
Markov Processes
Student Seminar in MCMC sampling
Stochastic Simulation
Clinical Biostatistics (UZH course)

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
Numerical Solutions of Stochastic Ordinary Differential Equations was super interesting, even though the teaching is not very good. If you can motivate yourself I would definitely recommend. 

I liked Markov Processes but it is a high workload for 3 credits if you want to understand the material. 

Causality is a must-take course if you have any interest in statistics - very interesting and well taught. I would in general also recommend doing a seminar as it is a good way to meet people and see some research. In addition there is no exam - which you will appreciate during the exam season. 

Stochastic Simulation was a good intro to a lot of simulation (MCMC) stuff. There are a lot of topics however, and if you want things explained in depth, this is probably not the right course to take.

Clinical Biostatistics is very doable and probably practically relevant, but not very interesting from a mathematical standpoint. I only tookit to fill up some credits.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: You have to pay radio and television tax (similar to old licens in Denmark) which is about 1500 DKK per household per half year.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Having a mobile subscription was surprisingly expensive. Food is very expensive, especially if you eat meat/animal products.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I did not utilize theses.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: There is a lot of sports organized, but not anything i utilized.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Go out to the mountains! The nature is extremely beautiful.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: You likely wont have time to do anything but study.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Switzerland is essentially Denmark with a bit higher cost of living. Adjusting is very easy.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Seeing as I attended the autumn semester, I started the same time as a lot of new masters students. These are from all over the world, and dont know anyone either, so they are easy to socialize with if you attend the new students events in addition to the exchange student events.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: None

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: As mentioned above, the culture is very similar to Denmark so nothing particular to share here.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1. Be prepared to study (a lot).
2. Exams feel frustrating/unfair and you might think you have done poorly, but you have likely done better than you think.
3. People are a bit more competetive/intense at ETH, this is not necessarily because they are unfriendly.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Not that I have not already mentioned.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Having fun subjects that were academically challenging.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Managing taking 6 courses 5 of which corresponded to a UCPH course in curriculum covered.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: No.

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
